title: RBAC Drift Incident Runbook and Normalized SIEM Export
summary: Runbook for triaging and remediating incidents where RBAC changes or configuration drift appear correlated with suspicious activity; includes automated evidence snapshot procedures and the normalized mapping for SIEM export to support post-incident reconstruction and auditors.
objectives: 1. Provide runbook steps to detect and contain RBAC drift during an incident. 2. Enumerate automated evidence-capture commands and retention guidance. 3. Define normalized SIEM export fields and mapping for faster analyst work and auditor review.
scope: Applies to incidents where access-control anomalies (unexpected role grants, privilege escalation, unusual service-account bindings) are observed or suspected. Covers hosted control plane and Private deployments managed by Redwood security team; does not replace cloud-provider-specific IR runbooks but complements them with RBAC-focused evidence and SIEM normalization.
preconditions_and_assumptions: - Oncall has access to the security playbook Slack channel and to rbacctl scope:read, scope:snapshot. - SIEM ingestion supports JSON schema v2 normalization. - Teams maintain KMS-backed evidence store for snapshots. - This runbook expects at least one live telemetry signal (audit log alert, external report, or anomaly detection).
detection_signals: Possible triggers: 1) Spike in role.grant events in audit logs for admin/owner-like roles. 2) New service-account keys created outside of change window. 3) RBAC change events correlated with suspicious IPs or unusual hours. 4) Alerts from RBAC-drift detector job (rbac-drift-detector) or manual report from product teams.
immediate_actions_first_15_minutes: 1) Acknowledge and create incident ticket (Jira). 2) Short-circuit risky sessions: temporarily revoke recently granted high-privilege roles (if safe) or create deny policies via policy-engine. 3) Capture live snapshot: run rbacctl snapshot --incident <ID> --store=kms://evidence-bucket --note='initial-live-snapshot'. 4) Notify SRE and identity-owner oncall via PagerDuty channel. 5) Enable heightened audit-log retention and mark retention key in evidence store.
containment_guidance: - Conservative containment: disable suspicious tokens/keys and remove ephemeral grants created in last 1 hour. - Aggressive containment: revoke role bindings created in last 24 hours for accounts with activity flagged by threat intel. - Use canary rollback: if an automated rollout changed RBAC, rollback the rollout via release-engineering and mark change set.
evidence_capture_playbook: The goal is to capture authoritative, time-ordered artifacts with verifiable provenance. Steps: 1) RBAC API snapshot: rbacctl export --format=json --since='2026-02-24T00:00:00Z' --out=/tmp/<incident>-rbac.json; upload to kms://evidence-bucket/<incident>/rbac-initial.json and record checksum (sha256). 2) Audit logs slice: query audit-api '/v1/audit/logs?from=<t-48h>&to=<t+1h>&filter=resource.type:iam OR protoPayload.methodName:GrantRole' -> save to kms store. 3) Service-account keys: list keys for impacted service-accounts and call keyctl disable --id=<key-id> (if containment decided); capture key metadata to evidence store. 4) Token/session snapshots: call sessions export --user=<user> --since=...; persist header and IPs. 5) Network indicators and PCAPs: if applicable, request SRE to pull flow logs for relevant VPCs/time windows. 6) Keeper: write a provenance record including who ran each command, at what time, and the checksums of the artifacts. Use evidence-provenance template in confluence.
automation_snippets_and_examples:
(examples for oncall use; adapt to env)
- RBAC snapshot (single command): rbacctl snapshot --incident ${INCIDENT_ID} --out s3://evidence-bucket/${INCIDENT_ID}/rbac-snapshot.json --with-attachments=true
- Filtered audit export: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 'https://audit.redwood.ai/v1/exports?from=${T0}&to=${T1}&q=protoPayload.methodName:GrantRole' > /tmp/audit-slice.json
- Upload with provenance: evidence-uploader --file /tmp/audit-slice.json --incident ${INCIDENT_ID} --uploader "$USER" --key-enc=kms://redwood/evidence-key
- Run SIEM normalization (locally): siem-normalize --schema v2 --input /tmp/audit-slice.json --output /tmp/normalized.json
Note: these CLI names are placeholders tied to internal automation; if running in private deployments use the on-prem equivalents and record operator identity explicitly.
rbac_snapshot_contents_expected: Snapshot should include: 1) principal list (users, groups, service-accounts) with stable IDs, 2) role definitions and attached policies, 3) bindings (who->role->resource), 4) temporal metadata (created_at, modified_at), 5) change origin (API, console, IaC change-set id), 6) source IPs for binding operations if available.
siem_normalized_schema_overview: Purpose: provide a canonical minimal set of fields so SOC analysts and auditors can immediately correlate identity changes across systems. Required normalized fields: timestamp, event_id, actor_id (stable), actor_type (user|svc|group), action_type (grant|revoke|modify|create_key|disable_key), target_type (role|resource|key), target_id, change_origin (api|console|iac|automation), request_ip, request_user_agent (if present), related_incident_id, raw_payload_ref (evidence-bucket URI), checksum_sha256. Optional fields: policy_diff_summary, prior_binding_hash, cloud_provider_region.
siem_export_mapping_examples: Example mapping rules: 1) audit.protoPayload.methodName == 'GrantRole' -> action_type=grant, target_type=role, target_id=protoPayload.request.roleName. 2) api.event == 'serviceAccount.keys.create' -> action_type=create_key, target_type=key, target_id=protoPayload.response.name. 3) iam.binding.delete -> action_type=revoke, policy_diff_summary=diff_summary. For each mapping include raw_payload_ref pointing to the preserved JSON object in the evidence bucket and record the checksum.
post_incident_reconstruction_steps: 1) Assemble normalized SIEM timeline using normalized.event_id and timestamp. 2) Cross-link RBAC snapshot artifacts by principal stable ID and compute timeline of when bindings first/last changed. 3) Re-execute policy diff tool: policy-diff --before s3://evidence/<incident>/rbac-before.json --after s3://evidence/<incident>/rbac-after.json -> save diff summary. 4) Map suspicious actions to sessions and IPs and escalate to threat-hunting if IOC overlap found. 5) Produce reconstruction doc: include timeline, artifacts (with URIs and checksums), decisions made, and rationale for containment actions.
chain_of_custody_and_retention: - All artifacts stored in KMS-protected evidence-bucket with object metadata: uploader, timestamp, checksum, incident_id. - Write a custody log entry for each upload indicating who handled the artifact and why. - Retention: default 180 days for RBAC-related incident artifacts, extendable to 2 years for regulatory review. - For Private deployments coordinate retention with customer contract and on-prem evidence policies.
communication_and_escalation_matrix: - Level 1 (oncall sec): initial triage and capture. - Level 2 (sec lead + identity engineer): containment decisions for cross-team grants. - Level 3 (CISO + Legal): regulatory notification assessment (if PII/exfiltration suspected). - Notify product security and impacted product owners within 2 hours of confirmed privilege change affecting production. - Use '#sec-incident' Slack channel and the SEC pagerduty escalation policy.
audit_and_compliance_notes: - For auditors provide the normalized SIEM timeline, RBAC snapshots (before/after if available), provenance ledger, and commit IDs for any IaC rollbacks. - Include signatures (operator, reviewer) on the evidence-provenance record. - Maintain a compact executive summary suitable for legal with redaction notes for PII.
playback_and_postmortem_template: Attach the following to the incident ticket: 1) Executive summary (1 paragraph). 2) Timeline (UTC) with normalized events. 3) Key decisions and rationale. 4) Evidence manifest (list of URIs + checksums). 5) Root cause hypothesis and validation steps. 6) Action items (owners, due dates) for preventing RBAC drift recurrence (examples: add pre-commit policy tests, require 2FA for role grants, reduce long-lived keys).
open_questions_and_known_gaps: - We currently lack automated enforcement to prevent new grants outside of workflows (IaC/enforced change windows). - Some private deployments do not surface request IP in RBAC change events; plan to instrument agent. - SIEM normalization needs a standard for policy_diff_summary length/format so analytic queries remain performant.
references_and_templates: - Confluence: RBAC snapshot schema (SEC-RBAC-SCHEMA). - GitHub: infra/rbacctl (export and snapshot implementations). - Template: evidence-provenance.md in confluence. - Jira: SEC-1348 (RBAC drift detector backlog).
last_steps_and_runbook_closure: After incident closure, ensure: 1) Evidence retained per retention schedule. 2) Postmortem completed and reviewed within 10 business days. 3) Action items tracked and owned. 4) If a systemic issue found, raise a cross-team enforcement ticket with platform-engineering to prevent recurrence.
notes_to_future_oncall: When in doubt, prioritize evidence capture over blocking a change that might break production. Always get a second reviewer for any destructive remediation (mass revokes). Use the evidence uploader to attach provenance; it will simplify audits.
